message_4_subject: Re: Fwd: Checkout failures: initial findings — edge+retry amplification
message_4_body:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Checkout failures: initial findings — edge+retry amplification

Quick technical summary from infra triage:
- Observed concurrent 502 and 503 spikes across EU edges (FRA, AMS) starting ~08:38 UTC; a smaller correlated bump seen in us-west around 08:45 UTC.
- Edge LB returns are primarily 502 (upstream connection reset) — upstream replica pools experienced transient connection saturation.
- Logged client behavior: many clients (including Vireo SDK instances) retry aggressively (initial backoff 100-200ms, max retries 5) — retry waves match the 502 spikes.
- There are also bursts of path-specific cache-miss traffic that increase upstream open connection count and KV cache cold misses.

Immediate mitigations enacted (10:00 UTC):
1) Edge config: enabled per-source soft throttling for Vireo's CIDR to cap concurrent connections to upstream by 30% (short window)
2) Edge timeouts: extended upstream handshake timeout + added 500ms jitter to acceptance window to reduce synchronized retries
3) Gate-level: enabled a temporary 429-fallback that returns a short backoff header to clients rather than passing connection resets
4) Warmed hot prefixes and increased pool size for the affected model instances by 2 replicas in EU zone

Next steps (owner):
- Karthik: continue LB and k8s pod metric monitoring, keep kits open for 4 hours
- Marissa/Logan: communicate status to Vireo and confirm client retry config change (ask them to increase initial backoff to 500ms)
- Sean: prepare exec note if incident persists beyond 2 hours.

Preliminary conclusion: retry amplification + cache churn caused transient connection saturation at upstream, which produced 502s — client retries amplified the feedback loop. Mitigations above should dampen the wave within 30–60 minutes.

-Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

message_5_subject: [Exec] Vireo Retail — edge 502/503 surge (EU) — mitigation & ask
message_5_body:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: VP Operations <vp-ops@redwood.com>, VP Sales <vp-sales@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: [Exec] Vireo Retail — edge 502/503 surge (EU) — mitigation & ask

Team — FYI and quick ask. Vireo Retail is experiencing a production-impacting 502/503 surge in EU during their checkout flow. Root cause appears to be retry amplification coupled with cache cold misses leading to upstream connection saturation.

What we've done: per-customer soft-throttle, adjusted edge timeouts, enabled 429-fallback, warmed prefix caches, scaled model replica pools in EU. Visible error rates dropped from ~8% to ~1.6% over the last 25 minutes.

Immediate asks:
- Approve up to 2 hours of reserved burst capacity in EU (additional replicas and node pool scaling) — estimate cost impact: ~$1,800/hr for current sizing.
- Approve a one-time service credit for Vireo for the window 08:38–11:00 UTC (TBD amount) so CS can close the loop.

If we don't hear back within 30 minutes we'll enact a temporary credits offer per CS standard and continue mitigations.

I'll post a concise exec summary after stabilization. — Logan
